label: second token after a leading l, for 11 specific tokens
explanation: A bigram detector. It fires only at step 1 (the second original token) when the first token is l and the second token is one of {1, t, p, n, u, h, 2, q, k, e, j}. On dev it fires on every such case and never anywhere else. It never fires on the delimiter, during the copy phase, or at any other position, and it stays silent when l is followed by any other token (for example a, c, d, m, v, w). The activation depends only on the second token: 1 gives the max (0.117), u and p are also high, e and t are mid-range, and k and q are the weakest (about 0.22 of max). Sequence length has no effect beyond determining how often the bigram occurs.

issues: No refutation found. On test the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 (6172 active steps, 6172 predicted), and misses --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The other claims check out on the dev profile. Every activation is at t=1 (orig_idx 1). Activation is zero at the delimiter and in the copy phase. first_tok and prev_tok are l for all activations. Mean activation per token (mass share divided by count) is highest for 1, then u and p. t (0.57) and e (0.54) are mid-range, and k (0.22) and q (0.24) are the weakest, matching the explanation.

Minor note, not a defect: 'sequence length has no effect' holds for whether the feature fires. The by-L mass shares are about even (around 0.16 each from L=4 to L=9, and L=3 has fewer steps), so no length pattern shows up.
